note: Rough, typical figures, not measurements of any one network. Latencies are one-way milliseconds; a round trip is twice the sum along the way. Geography is about half the usual ping between two cities' internet exchanges; access is the last mile of one side.

datacenter.note: A server in a data centre: the relay.

lan.note: Two machines on one home network, used when both name the same lan.

cable.note: DOCSIS: low latency down, a narrow, jittery upstream.

adsl.note: ADSL2+ with interleaving: slow, and a 1 Mbit uplink.

4g.note: LTE on a decent signal: scheduler jitter and a little loss.

starlink.note: LEO satellite: low-ish latency that jumps at every satellite handover.

hotel-wifi.note: A shared, contended Wi-Fi: the travelling case.

geo-satellite.note: Geostationary satellite: the worst a host can sit behind.
